scopeDetail.supervisor: Existing PowerShell supervisor with its real workspace guard and three bounded monitoring cycles
scopeDetail.contention: Separate parent held the actual Windows lifecycle file lease. Fixture facade delegated recovery to the actual public command while held
scopeDetail.recovery: Isolated facade translated the post-lease recovery request into a fixture-owned headless launch. Native production startup uses fixed port 3200
scopeDetail.readiness: Existing PowerShell initialize and tools/list verifier used the real checkouts, exact candidate path and hash, and local TCP owner. Fixture owner validation admitted the supported headless process only on the assigned private port

firstAttempts: The supervisor ended after the native listener verifier rejected the headless executable, which correctly lacks the native daemon command flag. Initial ephemeral logs were removed. A diagnostic attempt reproduced and identified the refusal.
The first test-only headless owner adapter referred to a shadowed PowerShell endpoint variable. The final fixture binds the exact process record explicitly.
